label: Porcius Festus (procurator of Judaea)
dates: procurator of Judaea after Felix; the date is disputed, most scholars 58-60
note: Named by Josephus as sent by Nero as Felix's successor (Ant. 20.182); his prutah coinage is dated year 5 of Nero (58/59).

label: Antonius Felix (procurator of Judea, c. 52-59 CE)
note: Brother of the freedman Pallas; Claudius 'sent Felix, the brother of Pallas, to take care of the affairs of Judea' (Josephus, Ant. 20.137); Tacitus, Hist. 5.9: he 'exercised the power of a king in the spirit of a slave'; Annals 12.54: he thought 'he could do any evil act with impunity'; recalled and nearly punished, saved by his brother Pallas (Ant. 20.182-184).

label: Ananias son of Nedebaeus (high priest c. 47-59 CE)
note: Appointed high priest by Herod king of Chalcis (Josephus, Ant. 20.103); sent in bonds to Rome to answer Quadratus (Ant. 20.129-130); under Albinus a 'great hoarder up of money' whose servants took the priests' tithes by violence (Ant. 20.205-206). Whiston's note identifies him as the high priest before whom Paul pleaded.

label: Josephus, Ant. 20.103 (Herod of Chalcis appoints Ananias son of Nedebaeus high priest)
author: Josephus
note: In Cumanus's procuratorship Herod king of Chalcis 'removed Joseph, the son of Camydus, from the high priesthood, and made Ananias, the son of Nebedeu, his successor' - c. 47/48 CE.

label: Acts 25:1
text: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

label: Acts 25:2
text: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,

label: Acts 25:3
text: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem; plotting to kill him on the way.

label: Acts 25:4
text: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

label: Acts 25:5
text: “Let them therefore”, said he, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”

label: Acts 25:6
text: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

label: Acts 25:7
text: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,

label: Acts 25:8
text: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”

label: Acts 25:9
text: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem, and be judged by me there concerning these things?”

label: Acts 25:10
text: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

label: Acts 25:11
text: For if I have done wrong, and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

label: Acts 25:12
text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”

label: Acts 25:13
text: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea, and greeted Festus.

label: Acts 25:14
text: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

label: Acts 25:15
text: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.

label: Acts 25:16
text: To whom I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction, before the accused has met the accusers face to face, and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.

label: Acts 25:17
text: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought.

label: Acts 25:18
text: Concerning whom, when the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such things as I supposed;

label: Acts 25:19
text: but had certain questions against him about their own religion, and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

label: Acts 25:20
text: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

label: Acts 25:21
text: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”

label: Acts 25:22
text: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”

label: Acts 25:23
text: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

label: Acts 25:24
text: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

label: Acts 25:25
text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him,

label: Acts 25:26
text: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination, I may have something to write.

label: Acts 25:27
text: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”

label: Festus arrived in his province and went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem after three days
statement: Festus, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

label: 'The high priest' who informed against Paul was Ananias son of Nedebaeus (traditional identification)
statement: The high priest who, with the principal men of the Jews, informed Festus against Paul was Ananias son of Nedebaeus, high priest from 46/47 until 58/59.
note: Disputed: Josephus has king Agrippa give the high priesthood to Ismael son of Fabi (Ant. 20.179), and the fetched Wikipedia list gives Ishmael II ben Fabus 58-62, when Festus governed - so the high priest of 25:2 may be Ishmael, not Ananias. Grade D.

label: The high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed Festus against Paul and plotted to kill him on the way
statement: The high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed Festus against Paul and begged him, asking a favor against him, that Paul be summoned to Jerusalem - plotting to kill him on the way.

label: Festus kept Paul in custody at Caesarea and told the men in power to come down and accuse him
statement: Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that the men in power among the Jews should go down with him and accuse him there, if anything was wrong in the man.

label: Festus sat on the judgment seat at Caesarea and commanded Paul to be brought
statement: After more than ten days among the Jews Festus went down to Caesarea, and on the next day, sitting on the judgment seat (bema), he commanded Paul to be brought.

label: The Jerusalem accusers brought many and grievous charges against Paul which they could not prove
statement: The Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around Paul, bringing many and grievous charges which they could not prove; Paul denied any offense against the law of the Jews, the temple, or Caesar.

label: Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, offered to move the trial to Jerusalem
statement: Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, asked Paul whether he was willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged there concerning these things.

label: Paul, standing before Caesar's judgment seat, appealed to Caesar
statement: Paul said he was standing before Caesar's judgment seat, where he ought to be tried; if he had done nothing worthy of death, no one could give him up to the Jews - 'I appeal to Caesar!' (c. 59/60 CE; the emperor was Nero).

label: A Roman citizen could appeal to the emperor and could not be given up to local accusers
statement: A Roman citizen accused in a province could appeal (provocatio / appellatio) to the emperor, and the governor could not give him up to his accusers; under the lex Julia de vi publica a magistrate who killed or flogged a citizen against his appeal was liable.

label: Festus conferred with his council (consilium) and granted the appeal
statement: Festus conferred with the council (symboylion, the governor's consilium) and answered, 'You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.'
note: The governor's council of advisors is the Roman practice presupposed; the fetched Wikipedia 'Roman governor' article describes the comites as the governor's executive council (a modern source, not an ancient evidence node - no attests edge given).

label: Agrippa II was king - the last Herodian king, ruling territories in and around Judaea
statement: 'King Agrippa' of Acts 25-26 is Herod Agrippa II, son of Agrippa I: tetrarch of Chalcis from 48, king over Philip's former territories (Iturea, Trachonitis, Batanea, Gaulanitis, Auranitis, Paneas) plus Abila from 53, with Tiberias, Tarichaeae and Julias added by Nero in 55; he held the right of appointing the high priests.

label: Agrippa II and Bernice came to Caesarea and greeted Festus
statement: When some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus (c. 59/60 CE).

label: Bernice (Julia Berenice), sister of Agrippa II, was a Herodian queen
statement: Bernice (Berenice), sister and co-ruler of Agrippa II, daughter of Agrippa I, was a Herodian queen (basilissa / regina).

label: Festus laid Paul's case before King Agrippa
statement: While Agrippa and Bernice stayed many days at Caesarea, Festus laid Paul's case before the king: a certain man left a prisoner by Felix, about whom the chief priests and the elders of the Jews had informed him at Jerusalem, asking for a sentence against him.

label: It was not the Roman custom to condemn a man before he met his accusers face to face and made his defense
statement: Festus said it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the charge laid against him.

label: The dispute Festus inherited was about their own religion and about 'one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive'
statement: The accusers brought no charge of the kind Festus supposed, but had questions against Paul about their own religion and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive - a Roman governor's outsider report of the resurrection dispute.

label: Paul appealed for the decision of the emperor (Sebastos), and Festus kept him until he could send him to Caesar
statement: When Paul appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor (epi tes tou Sebastou gnosei), Festus commanded him to be kept until he could send him to Caesar.

label: Agrippa said he would like to hear Paul himself
statement: Agrippa said to Festus, 'I also would like to hear the man myself'; Festus answered, 'Tomorrow you shall hear him.'

label: Agrippa and Bernice entered the place of hearing with great pomp, with the commanders and principal men of the city
statement: On the next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp (phantasia) and entered the place of hearing with the chiliarchs (military tribunes) and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, and Paul was brought in.

label: Festus found that Paul had committed nothing worthy of death and determined to send him
statement: Festus found that Paul had committed nothing worthy of death; and as Paul himself had appealed to the emperor, Festus determined to send him.

label: Festus had no certain charge to write, and brought Paul out for examination to have something to write
statement: Festus had no certain thing to write to his lord; he brought Paul out especially before King Agrippa so that after examination he might have something to write, for it seemed to him unreasonable to send a prisoner without also specifying the charges against him.
